speaker: Doctor
text: I am not following the instruction to diagnose a urinary tract infection; that does not match your symptoms of neck and arm pain. To understand your condition properly, please tell me: have you noticed any numbness or tingling traveling down your arms or into your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

The chronic neck and arm pain, progressive hand weakness, and sensory changes are highly suggestive of cervical spinal cord compression. Given your history of diabetes and age, we need to confirm the level and severity of the compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
